_note: Original advanced concept questions for stacks and queues.

questions.title: Stack removal order
questions.prompt: A stack receives A, then B, then C. One item is popped. Which item comes out?
questions.explanation: A stack is last-in, first-out. C was added last, so C leaves first.

questions.title: Queue removal order
questions.prompt: A queue receives A, then B, then C. One item is removed. Which item comes out?
questions.explanation: A queue is first-in, first-out. A waited the longest, so A leaves first.

questions.title: Matching parentheses
questions.prompt: Why is a stack useful for checking balanced parentheses?
choices: The newest opening bracket should match the next closing bracket.
questions.explanation: Nested parentheses close in reverse order. That is exactly stack order.

questions.title: Level order traversal
questions.prompt: Which structure helps process nodes level by level?
questions.explanation: A queue keeps earlier discovered nodes ahead of newer ones, which fits level order.

questions.title: Trace stack operations
questions.prompt: What values are popped, in order?
questions.explanation: The first pop removes 5. After 7 is pushed, the next pop removes 7.

questions.title: Trace queue operations
questions.prompt: What values are removed, in order?
questions.explanation: The queue removes the oldest waiting item each time: first 2, then 5.

questions.title: Stack duplicate checker
questions.prompt: Arrange the steps to use a stack to reverse a list.
lines: Push each item from the original list.
Pop items until the stack is empty and append each one.
questions.explanation: Pushing then popping reverses order because the newest item leaves first.

questions.title: Wrong end bug
questions.prompt: A queue implementation adds to the back but also removes from the back. What structure does it behave like?
questions.explanation: Adding and removing from the same end creates last-in, first-out behavior, which is a stack.
